standard_prerequisites.name: A pair is henselian as soon as it is henselian with respect to every principal ideal generated by an element of the ideal
standard_prerequisites.use: Reduces the statement for the given ideal to the case of a single element.

standard_prerequisites.name: A complete ring with respect to a principal ideal forms a henselian pair, and a pair is henselian when its completion is and the kernel of the completion map is handled
standard_prerequisites.use: Transfers the property from the adic completion back to the ring through the two intermediate statements.

standard_prerequisites.name: A ring that is derived complete with respect to an element is derived complete, hence complete, with respect to the principal ideal that element generates
standard_prerequisites.use: Justifies applying the completeness statements to the principal ideal generated by the chosen element.

core_obligations: Reduce to a principal ideal: by the criterion for henselian pairs it suffices to show that the pair consisting of the ring and the ideal generated by an arbitrary element of the given ideal is henselian (proof lines 27092-27094).
Observe that the ring is derived complete, hence complete, with respect to that principal ideal, directly from the definition of derived completeness (proof lines 27094-27096).
Use the statement comparing a ring with its adic completion to see that the map from the ring to its completion with respect to the principal ideal is surjective (proof lines 27096-27098).
Apply the statement that the adic completion of a ring at a principal ideal forms a henselian pair, so the pair with the completion as the ring is henselian (proof lines 27098-27100).

Conclude that it suffices to show that the pair formed with the intersection of the powers of the ideal is henselian, and deduce that from the two statements about the kernel of the completion map and about locally nilpotent extensions (proof lines 27100-27104).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to a principal ideal generated by an element of the given ideal (proof lines 27092-27094).
Get completeness for that principal ideal from derived completeness and surjectivity onto the completion (proof lines 27094-27098).
Transfer henselianity from the completion and then from the intersection of the powers to the ring itself (proof lines 27098-27104).
